last_run: 'How sure are you?' now shows how far calls like yours landed, not just how often they won: a small bar and one line, e.g. 90-day bullish calls: the worst 1 in 10 ended 12 pts or more behind the S&P, the best 1 in 10 12 pts or more ahead, the middle call 2 pts behind.
next: After Monday's grading run (about 5:47 PM ET), check the spread bar shows in chat and on My calls, and the strategist yardsticks on /brain; then the Close Call records after the first grades on Nov 19.

replies.body: A 42% hit rate reads like a coin flip with small stakes. The base-rate line now also shows the range: about 12 pts either way vs the S&P for a single 90-day call, from the app's own graded calls.

A professor would ask 'compared to what?' about the strategists' +2.6 pts. The board now shows the app's own pick (+2.6) and a random idea (+0.3) on the same calls, so nobody mistakes a tie for a win.
A finance professor would ask how 114k picks got graded in two weeks. The Brain page now says it plainly: 5,474 real-time grades, the rest practice calls graded from history.

Close Call now shows each user their own record against the market's odds: 'You were right 7 of 14; the market's odds expected 6.7', with an honest skill-or-luck line. Each answer also shows the odds the market gave it.
